newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker, RGI agree to merge.
newsitem.headline: Aker, RGI agree to merge.

text.p: Norwegian engineering and offshore group Aker ASA said on Tuesday it had agreed to merge with investment group Resource Group International (RGI).
"The short version is that we are merging," Aker spokesman Frode Geitvik said.
A statement said the parties agreed on an exchange ratio of one Aker share to 2.15 RGI shares.

The news of the breakthrough in the merger talks followed statements by both companies on Monday morning that they had abandoned the effort to join forces because they were unable to agree on the exchange value of their shares.
Tuesday's statement said the merger means that RGI, which is registered in the Netherland Antilles, is moving its business formally to Norway.
It said the company boards had unanimously recommended a merger. The proposal needs final approval by shareholders of the two companies.
Aker said the fusion with RGI would form a company with annual revenues of about 19 billion crowns ($2.9 billion) and almost 17,000 employees.
Trawler-based RGI earlier this year acquired 30 percent of Aker shares and has options to buy nearly 10 percent more.
-- Rolf Soderlind, Oslo newsroom +47 22 42 50 41 ($ = 6.49 Norwegian Crowns)
